claims.text: A hybrid MLP and on-the-fly reweighting method can reliably reproduce solid- and liquid-phase free energies at fusion conditions.
The hybrid method can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The hybrid method can substantially reduce simulation cost relative to explicit AIMD.
MLPs trained on short, targeted AIMD trajectories can capture the relevant interatomic interactions and free-energy landscapes of both solid and liquid phases.
A reweighting or thermodynamic-integration correction during production runs can recover ab initio-level fidelity.
Augmenting the training set with AIMD configurations ensures accurate MLP representation of configurations in both phases.
Replacing costly AIMD trajectories with MLP production sampling accelerates configurational sampling.
A reduced set of ab initio evaluations can correct systematic MLP deviations in calculated free-energy differences.
The layered MLP and reweighting approach preserves vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration contributions without exhaustive AIMD.
The proposed method will be approximately 10–20 times faster than full AIMD free-energy evaluation.
The proposed method will outperform TOR-TILD for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method will produce free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats with errors similar to those of explicit AIMD.
Explicit AIMD free-energy evaluation is prohibitively costly for high-entropy and multicomponent systems.
TOR-TILD is effective for elemental and binary systems but experiences steep slowdowns in multicomponent systems.
The proposed method is expected to apply from elemental and binary systems through multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Performance may degrade outside the fusion-temperature region.
Performance may degrade when electron–vibration coupling exceeds current machine-learning representability.
